prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: one high-fidelity desktop homepage direction comp

Primary request: Create exactly one polished 1440x960 landscape first-viewport website comp for VIZ Creative, an Abuja interior-design and architectural-visualization studio. Direction name: “Model Room.” Draw lineage from architectural maquette studios, project pin-up walls, and exhibition plinths. The result must be a premium, shippable studio portfolio website viewed straight-on—not a mood board, poster, brand board, browser mockup, or standalone illustration.

Input images: Image 1 is the real existing VIZ Creative hero render and must be the dominant media. Preserve the complete image exactly as a recognizable architectural render: white arched commercial complex, blue sky, palms, cars, paving, and foreground. Show the whole source image with no cropping inside a true 16:9 media frame. Because the source is 4:3, use object-fit contain on a clean solid matte-black or museum-board backing, with honest flat margins where necessary; do not invent, stretch, blur, mirror, or crop image content and do not use blurry filler.

Product and interaction structure:
- Exact desktop webpage impression, 1440x960.
- A slim, practical top navigation around 60–68px high.
- Brand text exactly: “VIZ CREATIVE”.
- Navigation labels exactly once each: “Work”, “Services”, “About”.
- One clear primary action exactly: “Start a project”.
- First event is an expanding hero: show a dominant framed 16:9 project image in its poised pre-expansion state, clearly designed to enlarge smoothly toward the viewport when engaged. Express this through confident scale, edge alignment, a restrained text affordance such as “View project”, and a subtle progress or frame cue—not a fake device frame.
- Keep the studio copy compact and subordinate to the work, in a narrow information block rather than a conventional oversized marketing hero.
- Compact headline text exactly: “Spaces considered. Futures made visible.”
- Offer text exactly: “Interior design and architectural visualisation from Abuja.”
- Include a quiet factual hero caption such as “Commercial complex — Abuja” and “Architectural visualisation”.
- Show a deliberate glimpse of the next scroll section at the bottom, headed “Selected work”, with the top edges of pinned project plates or a project index visible.
- Preserve an obvious reading order and plausible clickable controls.

Model Room visual world:
- Museum-board page field with crisp structural divisions inspired by pin-up walls.
- One or two thin birch-ply ledges or exhibition-plinth planes, used as real compositional supports rather than decorative furniture.
- Project information appears as flat pinned sheets, caption slips, or flush wall labels; asymmetrical but rigorously aligned.
- Matte aluminium edges and graphite rules; square corners; tactile material realism kept restrained.
- Palette strictly led by museum board #d8d4ca, matte black #151615, graphite #6c6b64, and one warm marker #d99b2b.
- Use the warm marker only for one navigation/action detail and one tiny project locator or pin.
- Compact contemporary sans-serif typography, medium and small sizes, clear hierarchy, generous spacing; no giant headline.
- Quiet museum daylight and precise physical texture, but the interface must remain crisp and clearly digital.
- Experience-mode portfolio: the work itself leads within the first viewport; interface recedes.

Text fidelity: Render all specified text verbatim and legibly. Do not invent awards, metrics, testimonials, clients, commercial claims, slogans, project outcomes, or extra navigation.

Constraints: straight-on flat webpage capture; crisp 1440x960 desktop proportions; functional UI hierarchy; one visible “Start a project” action; no browser chrome; no watermark; no fake brand marks.

Avoid: technical instruments, drafting tools, rulers, compasses, blueprints, nautical navy or lime, glass, gradients, glow, blur, glassmorphism, excessive shadows, fake claims, awards, metrics, testimonials, logos, huge typography, serif display type, pill controls, rounded card grids, generic luxury styling, mood-board collage, poster composition, cropped hero image, stretched hero image, blurry side fills, duplicated source imagery.
